classification_signals: The paper includes sections like 'Review of Related Literature', 'Conceptual Frame Work', and 'Fact Finding on Aesthetic Considerations in Architectural Design' which synthesize existing research.

It explicitly states in the 'Purpose of the Study' that 'Through empirical research and case studies, this investigation aims to provide a deeper understanding...', but no such methods or results are presented within the paper itself, indicating it is a review of the field rather than new empirical work.
The 'Conclusion' section summarizes the findings from the literature review without introducing new data or analyses.
The 'Recommendations' section provides prescriptive advice based on the synthesized literature.
title: Aesthetic Considerations in Architectural Design: Exploring Pleasure, Arousal, and Dominance

findings.antecedent: Architectural aesthetics (form, materiality, color, lighting, spatial organization)
findings.consequent: Pleasure (delight, comfort, satisfaction), well-being, sense of belonging
findings.source: Abstract
findings.quote: Achieving pleasurable architecture necessitates meticulous attention to elements such as form, materiality, color, lighting, and spatial organization, culminating in an atmosphere that nurtures well-being and fosters a sense of belonging within the architectural space.

findings.antecedent: Architectural aesthetics (dynamic elements, spatial composition, movement, patterns, contrasts)
findings.consequent: Arousal (excitement, stimulation, engagement, intrigue, mystery, dynamism, tranquility, calmness)
findings.source: Abstract
findings.quote: Striking a balance in arousal levels is vital to creating spaces that are engaging without overwhelming occupants, encouraging them to actively explore and interact with the environment.

findings.antecedent: Architectural aesthetics (scale, material selection, form, geometry)
findings.consequent: Dominance (visual impact, power, control, hierarchy, symbolic identity, city character)
findings.source: Abstract
findings.quote: Dominance in architectural design centers on the visual impact of a building or structure within its surroundings. Dominant architectural landmarks often become symbolic identities that shape the character of a city or community.

findings.antecedent: Aesthetically pleasing architectural elements (green spaces, visually appealing facades)
findings.consequent: Positive emotional states, emotional well-being, overall satisfaction
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 4 (Joye and van den Berg, 2011)
findings.quote: aesthetically pleasing architectural elements, such as green spaces and visually appealing facades, positively influenced the participants' emotional states.

findings.antecedent: Visual complexity of architectural spaces
findings.consequent: Emotional responses (discomfort, dissatisfaction for overly complex; positive for moderately complex)
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 4 (Nasar and Julian, 1995)
findings.quote: overly complex designs could lead to feelings of discomfort and dissatisfaction, while moderately complex spaces were associated with positive emotional experiences.

findings.antecedent: Beautiful architectural designs
findings.consequent: Activation of brain regions associated with reward and positive emotions, pleasure centers
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Vartanian et al., 2013)
findings.quote: beautiful architectural designs activated brain regions associated with reward and positive emotions, indicating that aesthetic appeal in architecture has a measurable impact on the brain's pleasure centers.

findings.antecedent: Well-designed healthcare spaces (aesthetically pleasing, calming elements)
findings.consequent: Reduced stress levels, increased patient satisfaction
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Huisman et al., 2012)
findings.quote: well-designed healthcare spaces, featuring aesthetically pleasing and calming elements, contributed to reduced stress levels and increased patient satisfaction.

findings.antecedent: Visually stimulating and harmonious natural environments
findings.consequent: Feelings of relaxation and restoration
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Joye, 2007)
findings.quote: visually stimulating and harmonious natural environments promoted feelings of relaxation and restoration, emphasizing the significance of aesthetic considerations in creating restorative architectural spaces.

findings.antecedent: Interior design (warm color palettes, soft textures, personalized decor)
findings.consequent: Higher sense of pleasure, comfort, attachment to home
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Horelli et al., 2016)
findings.quote: the use of warm color palettes, soft textures, and personalized decor contributed to a higher sense of pleasure, comfort, and attachment to the home.

findings.antecedent: Well-designed educational spaces (natural light, vibrant colors, interactive learning areas)
findings.consequent: Students' engagement, pleasure in learning process, well-being, academic performance
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Lozano et al., 2017)
findings.quote: well-designed educational spaces, incorporating natural light, vibrant colors, and interactive learning areas, positively influenced students' engagement and pleasure in the learning process.

findings.antecedent: Sensory and emotional design (in products and spaces)
findings.consequent: Pleasurable experiences, positive emotions, increased user satisfaction, attachment
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Mugge and Schifferstein, 2004)
findings.quote: sensory and emotional design in creating pleasurable experiences, demonstrating that well-designed products and spaces can evoke positive emotions, leading to increased user satisfaction and attachment.

findings.antecedent: Design features (natural elements)
findings.consequent: Pleasure across cultures (universal effect), cultural differences in aesthetic preferences
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Vartanian et al., 2019)
findings.quote: while some design features, such as natural elements, tended to evoke pleasure across cultures, cultural differences influenced preferences for specific aesthetic elements.

findings.antecedent: Architectural complexity (moderately complex exhibits)
findings.consequent: Higher levels of arousal, interest, engaging and enjoyable museum experience
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Joye and Dewitte, 2018)
findings.quote: moderately complex exhibits evoked higher levels of arousal and interest in visitors, leading to a more engaging and enjoyable museum experience.

findings.antecedent: Visual complexity (moderate vs. overly complex)
findings.consequent: Aesthetic judgments, approach/avoidance behaviors (more pleasing/inviting for moderate; lower aesthetic judgment/increased avoidance for overly complex)
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Vartanian et al., 2013)
findings.quote: buildings with moderate visual complexity were perceived as more pleasing and inviting, leading to higher approach behaviors. On the other hand, overly complex designs resulted in lower aesthetic judgments and increased avoidance tendencies...

findings.antecedent: Spatial enclosure (moderately enclosed spaces)
findings.consequent: Activation of brain regions associated with feelings of safety and comfort, positive emotional experience, increased arousal
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 5 (Khalili-Mahani et al., 2017)
findings.quote: moderately enclosed spaces activated brain regions associated with feelings of safety and comfort, suggesting that the optimal level of spatial enclosure can contribute to a positive emotional experience and increased arousal in occupants.

findings.antecedent: Well-designed retail spaces (carefully controlled atmospherics: lighting, music, interior design)
findings.consequent: Higher levels of arousal, increased interest, exploration by customers
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Yalçın and Yücel, 2019)
findings.quote: well-designed retail spaces with carefully controlled atmospherics elicited higher levels of arousal, leading to increased interest and exploration by customers.

findings.antecedent: Environments with optimal sensory variety and moderate arousal levels
findings.consequent: Perceived preference, greater stress reduction
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Jain and Kaplan, 2008)
findings.quote: environments with optimal sensory variety and moderate arousal levels were perceived as more preferred and contributed to greater stress reduction.

findings.antecedent: Iconic structures (historic buildings, modern skyscrapers)
findings.consequent: Defining city's character, fostering sense of pride and attachment among residents
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Mavridou and Michailidou, 2016)
findings.quote: iconic structures, such as historic buildings or modern skyscrapers, play a crucial role in defining a city's character and fostering a sense of pride and attachment among its residents.

findings.antecedent: Dominant landmarks
findings.consequent: Higher preference, sense of orientation, identity within urban landscape
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Kaplan and Kaplan, 1982)
findings.quote: landmarks with a dominant presence were more likely to be preferred by individuals, as they provided a sense of orientation and identity within the urban landscape.

findings.antecedent: Dominant architectural forms
findings.consequent: Aesthetic preferences (similar responses across cultures for some features, cultural differences for others)
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Vartanian et al., 2016)
findings.quote: while some architectural features elicited similar responses across cultures, cultural differences influenced the perception of dominance and its aesthetic appeal.

findings.antecedent: Dominant landmarks (iconic architecture)
findings.consequent: Attracted tourists, economic growth (increased tourism revenue)
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Zhang and Kim, 2018)
findings.quote: dominant landmarks, such as famous buildings or unique structures, attracted tourists and contributed to economic growth through increased tourism revenue.

findings.antecedent: Integration of dominant architectural structures within historical urban environments (balancing historical context with new dominant buildings)
findings.consequent: Complement and enhance existing urban fabric, rather than overshadowing it
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Petiot et al., 2014)
findings.quote: preserving historical context while introducing new dominant buildings, ensuring that they complement and enhance the existing urban fabric rather than overshadowing it.

findings.antecedent: Street tree planting (lush greenery, aesthetically pleasing landscapes)
findings.consequent: Lower stress levels, enhanced well-being among residents
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Nasar and Kang, 2013)
findings.quote: streets with lush greenery and aesthetically pleasing landscapes were associated with lower stress levels and enhanced well-being among residents.

findings.antecedent: Window views of natural elements (greenery, water bodies) in office environments
findings.consequent: Reduced stress, improved concentration, enhanced well-being, productivity
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Herzog et al., 2004)
findings.quote: employees with views of natural elements, such as greenery or water bodies, experienced reduced stress and improved concentration compared to those without such views.

findings.antecedent: Aesthetically pleasing hotel environments
findings.consequent: Higher guest satisfaction, intentions to revisit
findings.source: Review of Related Literature, p. 6 (Reisinger et al., 2009)
findings.quote: aesthetically pleasing hotel environments were associated with higher guest satisfaction and intentions to revisit.

findings.antecedent: Harmonious proportions (relationships between elements, spatial configurations)
findings.consequent: Sense of visual order, coherence, pleasure
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 7 (Nasar & Terzano, 2016)
findings.quote: Harmonious relationships between elements, such as doorways, windows, and overall spatial configurations, create a sense of visual order and coherence, which can be inherently pleasing to individuals.

findings.antecedent: Color schemes (warm/inviting vs. vibrant/dynamic)
findings.consequent: Feelings of comfort/coziness vs. excitement/energy, pleasure
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 7 (Joye, 2007)
findings.quote: Warm and inviting color palettes can evoke feelings of comfort and coziness, while vibrant and dynamic colors can stimulate excitement and energy.

findings.antecedent: Variety of textures (soft fabrics, smooth surfaces, rough materials)
findings.consequent: Engagement of sense of touch, enhanced tactile experience, pleasurable environment
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 7 (Gifford, 2007)
findings.quote: Incorporating a variety of textures, such as soft fabrics, smooth surfaces, or rough materials, can engage the sense of touch and enhance the tactile experience of architectural spaces, contributing to a more pleasurable environment.

findings.antecedent: Lighting design (natural daylight, well-designed artificial lighting)
findings.consequent: Warm and inviting environment, enhanced pleasurable experience
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 7 (Herzog et al., 1997)
findings.quote: Natural daylight and well-designed artificial lighting can create a warm and inviting environment, enhancing the overall pleasurable experience.

findings.antecedent: Balance between familiarity and novelty in architectural design
findings.consequent: Comfort, security (familiar); excitement, interest, curiosity, imagination (novel); pleasure
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 7 (Knight & Haslam, 2010)
findings.quote: Familiar elements provide a sense of comfort and security, as they align with individuals' existing mental models and expectations. On the other hand, incorporating novel and innovative design features introduces excitement and interest, engaging users' curiosity and imagination.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic elements (moving artworks, water features, kinetic sculptures)
findings.consequent: Arousal, immersive and interactive experience, excitement, wonder
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 8 (Vartanian et al., 2013)
findings.quote: Elements such as moving artworks, water features, or kinetic sculptures can instill a sense of excitement and wonder, enticing individuals to explore and engage with the architectural space.

findings.antecedent: Spatial composition (strategic arrangement of spaces, circulation paths)
findings.consequent: Sense of progression, visually stimulating experiences, narrative unfolding, attention capture, arousal
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 8 (Joye & De Block, 2011)
findings.quote: The strategic arrangement of spaces and circulation paths can create a sense of progression, leading users through a sequence of visually stimulating experiences, unfolding the narrative and capturing their attention at every turn.

findings.antecedent: Movement (dynamic views of nature, panoramas, framed vistas)
findings.consequent: Sense of awe and wonder, attention capture, emotional responses, arousal
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 8 (Herzog et al., 1997)
findings.quote: Dynamic views of nature, such as panoramas or framed vistas of natural landscapes, can create a sense of awe and wonder, capturing the viewers' attention and invoking emotional responses.

findings.antecedent: Patterns (intriguing patterns)
findings.consequent: Arousal, visual interest, complexity, mesmerizing effect, lingering, exploration
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 8 (Vartanian et al., 2019)
findings.quote: Intriguing patterns can create a mesmerizing effect, enticing viewers to linger and explore the intricacies of the design.

findings.antecedent: Contrasting elements (old/new styles, light/shadow play, natural/man-made materials)
findings.consequent: Tension, curiosity, suspense, heightened arousal
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 8 (Vartanian et al., 2013)
findings.quote: Contrasting elements in architectural design can evoke tension, curiosity, and suspense, thus heightening arousal.

findings.antecedent: Scale of architectural elements (large, imposing structures)
findings.consequent: Perceived dominance, command attention, sense of power and authority
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 8 (Nasar & Terzano, 2016)
findings.quote: large and imposing structures tend to command attention and convey a sense of power and authority.

findings.antecedent: Material selection (robust/monumental materials like stone/concrete vs. reflective/polished surfaces)
findings.consequent: Visual weight, elegance, sophistication, perceived dominance
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 9 (Joye, 2007)
findings.quote: Robust and monumental materials, such as stone or concrete, can enhance a structure's visual weight, while reflective or polished surfaces can add a sense of elegance and sophistication.

findings.antecedent: Form of architectural elements (bold, iconic forms)
findings.consequent: Dominance, stand out prominently
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 9 (Gifford, 2007)
findings.quote: Bold and iconic forms may stand out prominently, while complex geometries can add visual interest and create a sense of uniqueness.

findings.antecedent: Geometry (symmetry vs. asymmetry)
findings.consequent: Perception of dominance, stability/control (symmetry); dynamism/creative energy (asymmetry)
findings.source: Conceptual Frame Work, p. 9 (Vartanian et al., 2013)
findings.quote: Symmetrical compositions often convey a sense of stability and control, while asymmetrical arrangements may evoke dynamism and creative energy.

minimum_safe_summary: This narrative review synthesizes existing literature on aesthetic considerations in architectural design, focusing on the psychological and emotional impact of pleasure, arousal, and dominance. Key findings indicate that aesthetically pleasing elements like green spaces, harmonious proportions, and balanced complexity enhance positive emotions, reduce stress, and improve well-being. Arousal is influenced by dynamic elements, spatial composition, and patterns, with moderate complexity being optimal for engagement. Dominance is conveyed through scale, materials, form, and geometry, contributing to urban identity and preference, though cultural context modulates these effects. The paper emphasizes the importance of integrating these aesthetic dimensions with human psychology to create user-centric and impactful architectural spaces. No specific limitations of the review itself are stated.
